C1.rationale: Constraints are proportionate: the two hard ones (heredoc quoting, and stopping when the PR-sync verdict is not in_sync) are contract/irreversibility matters and both state why, but the closing numbered 'Best Practices' list is generic imperative guidance restating defaults a capable model already applies (imperative mood, 72-char subjects, always reference issues), which keeps it at competent rather than exemplary.

C2.rationale: The vocabulary the skill actually exposes is enumerated at the point of declaration rather than taught by accumulated examples: nine commit types with use case and version bump, and three issue-reference keywords with their exact effect; the single retained example (the heredoc block) covers a genuine ambiguity rather than restating the interface. Short of 5 because the enumeration is a copy of a table owned elsewhere and no invalid combinations are named.

C3.rationale: The body is a lean 5.8k-char entry point that carries only the core commit path and defers each rarer branch to a separately-loadable surface named explicitly — trailers to git-commit-trailers, issue matching to github-issue-autodetect, remote work to git-push/git-pr, branch reality to /git:pr-sync-check. Short of 5 only because nothing is bundled as an executable or reference artifact of its own.

evidence.quote: For trailer conventions (Co-authored-by, Signed-off-by, BREAKING CHANGE, Release-As), see **git-commit-trailers** skill.

C4.rationale: Three copies rather than pointers: the nine-row conventional-commit type table and the Fixes/Closes/Refs table are both restated here while `.claude/rules/conventional-commits.md` owns them (the skill links to that owner one line after copying it, and github-pr-title/SKILL.md carries the same type table), and the frontmatter description's trigger phrases are restated verbatim in the body's trigger-phrase list. Pointers dominate elsewhere, which keeps it above 1.

C5.rationale: C5 applies only to always-loaded surfaces (CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/*). This is a SKILL.md body that costs tokens only once the skill fires.

C6.rationale: The deterministic parts are given as exact runnable artifacts rather than described in prose — porcelain-v2 status, pre-commit invocation, and a copy-pasteable quoted-heredoc commit template that encodes the escaping trap it warns about — and the unit is unambiguous that these are to be run. Short of 5 because the issue-matching step remains prose confidence heuristics with no script or fixture, and the skill's own evals.json sits beside it unreferenced.

top_finding: Delete the conventional-commit type table and the Fixes/Closes/Refs table from the body and keep only the existing one-line pointer to `.claude/rules/conventional-commits.md`, which already owns both and is loaded anyway.
counter_finding: The quoted-heredoc warning earns its tokens outright — it names a real, non-obvious failure (a reflexive backslash-escape surviving into `git log` and needing an `--amend`) that a model would otherwise reproduce every time.

leakage.note: skill-quality.md and skill-development.md were auto-injected before I read the rubric, despite the instruction not to read them — I could not prevent that. I scored strictly against the rubric anchors: I gave no credit for the mandatory `## When to Use This Skill` table or for the absence of an Agentic Optimizations table, and I ignored char-count thresholds (C3 was scored on disclosure structure, i.e. named deferrals to sibling skills, not on the 10,000-char target). Where a house artifact was scorable under a published property I said so explicitly: the duplicated when-to-use surfaces counted under C4 single-sourcing, not as house non-compliance. conventional-commits.md was used only as C4 evidence of where the duplicated table is owned, which the rubric explicitly permits discovering via repo search.
